summary.text: The ocean is the body of salt water covering about 70.8% of Earth, conventionally split into the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Antarctic/Southern and Arctic oceans.
Holding 97% of Earth's water, it acts as a huge heat reservoir for Earth's energy budget, carbon cycle and water cycle, shaping climate and weather worldwide.
It harbours most of Earth's animals, originated photosynthesis and so the oxygen in our air, and still supplies half of that oxygen.

facts.label: "World Ocean" coined by
facts.value: Russian oceanographer Yuly Shokalsky, early 20th century

items.prompt: Today, about half the oxygen in the air you breathe is supplied by one source. Which is it?

options.label: Tropical rainforests
Grasslands and farm crops
The ocean
Volcanic gases

items.explain: The ocean originated photosynthesis and Earth's atmospheric oxygen, and it still supplies half of that oxygen.

items.prompt: A diver heads down from the sunny surface into deep water. Below which point can algae no longer use sunlight to make food?

options.label: Where light falls to about 1% of the surface value
Where the water first starts to feel cold
Exactly at the ocean floor, however deep
Just below the first few meters of water

items.explain: The photic zone, where photosynthesis can occur, reaches down to where light is only 1% of its surface value, roughly 200 m in the open ocean.

items.prompt: Where in the ocean would you expect the greatest variety of life and the base of most of its food?

options.label: The cold, dark deep ocean
The bottom mud of the deepest trenches
The layer under polar sea ice
The sunlit upper layer

items.explain: Because photosynthesis happens there, the photic zone is the most biodiverse and the source of the food that sustains most of the ocean ecosystem.

items.prompt: As people burn more fossil fuels, what happens to seawater's chemistry?

options.label: It becomes saltier
Its pH drops as it absorbs more CO₂
It loses all its dissolved nitrogen
Its pH rises as it releases CO₂

items.explain: Rising atmospheric CO₂, mainly from fossil fuels, is absorbed by the ocean and leads to acidification, a drop in pH.

items.prompt: You swim at the surface in the tropics and then dive to the deep sea far below. Roughly how cold does the deep water get?

options.label: About the same as the surface, near 30 °C
Around 15 to 20 °C
Between about −2 °C and 5 °C
Well below −20 °C

items.explain: Tropical surfaces can top 30 °C, but deep ocean temperatures everywhere range between −2 °C and 5 °C.

items.prompt: A friend calls the Red Sea "an ocean". Strictly speaking, what makes a sea different?

options.label: A sea is fresh water, not salt
A sea is partly or fully enclosed by land
A sea is deeper than any ocean
A sea has no currents or tides

items.explain: Strictly, a sea is a body of water partly or fully enclosed by land, generally smaller, though there is no sharp line between seas and oceans.

beats.title: Half Your Air Is Seawater
beats.hook: The ocean still supplies half the oxygen in the air you breathe.

beats.prompt: Put these oceans in order by area
beats.explain: Listed by descending area, the Pacific is largest and the Arctic smallest.

beats.prompt: Sunlight fades quickly with depth. Where in the ocean would most of its food supply be made?
beats.explain: Photosynthesis happens only in the photic zone, so it is the most biodiverse and the source of most of the ocean's food.

choices.label: On the ocean floor
choices.feedback: Below the top few hundred meters the ocean is dark, so algae there cannot use light.

choices.label: In the cold, dark deep water
choices.feedback: The deep ocean is dark, and without light, algae cannot photosynthesize.

choices.label: Evenly at every depth
choices.feedback: Light reaches only a few hundred meters, so food-making is not even.

beats.prompt: Match each ocean zone to its description

right.label: Open water from surface to floor

beats.explain: The water column is divided by depth and how much sunlight reaches it, from the sunlit photic zone down to the dark aphotic zone.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?

steps.text: Burning fossil fuels raises CO₂ in the air.
The ocean absorbs CO₂ from the atmosphere.
More CO₂ makes seawater less acidic, raising its pH.
This is one of the ways climate change affects the ocean.

beats.explain: A higher CO₂ concentration leads to ocean acidification, which is a drop in pH, not a rise.

beats.idea: The ocean holds most of Earth's water, stores heat, moves it around with currents and feeds most of its life from its sunlit upper layer.
